idiom_name: service class with constructor-injected abstract ports + RAII transaction guard
implementation_notes: The service is an ordinary class taking its collaborators as references, abstract base classes or std::function callbacks in the constructor, wired in the composition root, because C++ has neither a dependency-injection container nor declarative transactions. The unit of work becomes a small RAII guard that begins in its constructor and rolls back in its destructor unless commit() was called (cppreference's RAII pattern); the error channel is std::expected<T, E> (C++23) where exceptions are disabled or unwanted, and exceptions otherwise. The classic structure is the language's own idiom here - nothing replaces it - so the cost is genuine: one class, one guard and one error convention to maintain.
pitfalls: The RAII guard's commit must not run after the transaction handle is destroyed, and a destructor that throws during unwinding terminates the process; keep commit() explicit and noexcept.
Members that are references to repositories shorter-lived than the service dangle; document ownership at the composition root or hold unique_ptr references explicitly.
Mixing std::expected returns with enabled exceptions gives two error channels; pick one and translate at the boundary.
